summary: AI observability has become essential as LLM deployments scale, with the market growing to an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and projected to reach $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR. Without proper monitoring, teams face runaway API costs, degraded response quality, and blind spots in agent behavior that are nearly impossible to debug after the fact. Gartner predicts that by 2028, LLM observability investments will account for 50% of all GenAI deployments, up from just 15% in early 2026.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chain execution, prompt inputs/outputs, evaluation runs, and agent step-by-step reasoning for LangChain-based applications
features: Deep LangChain and LangGraph integration
Rich debugging and trace visualization
Evaluation framework with human and automated feedback
Dataset management and regression testing
Prompt versioning and comparison
Team collaboration and annotation tools
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39/seat/month with overage around $2.50 per thousand traces; Enterprise custom pricing. Approximately £80/month for 100K requests.
tools.best_for: Teams building with LangChain or LangGraph who need rich debugging, evaluation pipelines, and a tightly integrated development workflow

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, token usage, cost per request, latency, error rates, and prompt templates across providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, and others
features: One-line proxy setup requiring minimal code changes
Real-time cost tracking and spend dashboards
Request caching to reduce redundant API calls
Rate limiting and user-level usage tracking
Prompt versioning and A/B testing
SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance on Team tier
Open-source and self-hostable
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier at 10K requests/month; Pro at $79/month (unlimited seats, usage-based beyond included volume); Team at $799/month (adds SOC-2 and HIPAA); Enterprise custom. Approximately £20/month for 100K requests.
tools.best_for: Teams prioritizing cost visibility and optimization with minimal setup overhead, especially those calling multiple LLM providers and needing immediate spend control

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, model inputs/outputs, evaluation metrics, experiment runs, dataset versions, and end-to-end ML pipeline performance
features: Experiment tracking and model versioning inherited from W&B core
LLM trace logging via Weave product
Evaluation framework with custom scoring functions
Dataset and artifact management
Collaborative dashboards and reports
Integration with popular ML frameworks and LLM providers
tools.pricing: Free tier available for individuals; Team plans start at $50/seat/month; Enterprise pricing available. Existing W&B subscribers can extend to LLM monitoring within their current plan.
tools.best_for: ML teams already using W&B for traditional model training who want a unified platform covering both classical ML experiments and LLM observability without adopting a separate tool

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: LLM traces, embedding drift, retrieval quality in RAG pipelines, model performance degradation, hallucination rates, and enterprise-scale telemetry
features: Long-standing ML monitoring extended to LLMs
Arize Phoenix open-source tracing and evaluation engine
RAG pipeline observability including retrieval and reranking steps
OpenTelemetry-native instrumentation
Embedding visualization and drift detection
Integration with Databricks, Snowflake, and major cloud platforms
Enterprise RBAC and audit logging
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is free and open-source (source-available license). Arize AI managed platform offers a free Developer tier; Growth and Enterprise tiers are custom-priced based on volume and features.
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams needing robust telemetry, RAG-specific observability, and a platform that bridges traditional ML monitoring with LLM observability at scale

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, prompt versions, token usage, cost per trace, evaluation scores, and user session activity across any LLM provider
features: Open-source with active community and self-hosting option
Detailed trace and span visualization
Built-in and custom evaluation scoring
Prompt management with versioning and deployment
Dataset creation from production traces for testing
SDKs for Python, JavaScript, and OpenTelemetry
Integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and others
tools.pricing: LangFuse Cloud free for under 50K requests/month; paid cloud tiers available (approximately £20 for 500K requests). Self-hosted is free with infrastructure costs around £30/month plus roughly 2 hours of maintenance per month.
tools.best_for: Open-source-first teams wanting full control over their data through self-hosting, or cost-conscious teams needing solid tracing and evaluation without high SaaS fees

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, token counts, latency, and model metadata via OpenTelemetry-standard instrumentation across any LLM provider or framework
features: OpenTelemetry-native SDK for standardized tracing
Drop-in instrumentation for OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and more
Framework support for LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack, and others
Vendor-agnostic: exports to any OTel-compatible backend
Lightweight with minimal performance overhead
Open-source under Apache 2.0 license
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free. Backend storage and visualization costs depend on the chosen OTel-compatible platform (e.g., OpenObserve, Grafana, Datadog).
tools.best_for: Engineering teams that want vendor-neutral, standards-based LLM instrumentation and already operate an OpenTelemetry-compatible observability stack

tools.name: OpenObserve
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt inputs/outputs, cost and token metrics, infrastructure logs, application metrics, and frontend (RUM) monitoring in a unified platform
features: Unified LLM and infrastructure observability in a single deployment
Logs, metrics, traces, and RUM monitoring without separate tooling
OpenTelemetry-compatible ingestion
Prompt tracing and cost tracking
Online evaluations support
Significant cost savings versus Datadog at scale
Open-source with self-hosting option
tools.pricing: Open-source self-hosted version is free. Cloud pricing is consumption-based; significantly cheaper than Datadog for high-volume deployments. Enterprise pricing available.
tools.best_for: Teams tired of maintaining a separate DevOps telemetry stack alongside a dedicated LLM tool, who want unified infrastructure and LLM observability in one deployment

tools.name: Confident AI (DeepEval)
tools.monitors: LLM output quality, hallucination, answer relevancy, faithfulness, contextual precision and recall, toxicity, bias, and 50+ research-backed evaluation metrics
features: 50+ evaluation metrics open-sourced through DeepEval
Used by OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft teams
Evaluation integrated directly into the observability layer
Regression testing and CI/CD pipeline integration
Dataset management for benchmark creation
Real-time production monitoring with metric alerts
Red-teaming and safety evaluation capabilities
tools.pricing: DeepEval is open-source and free. Confident AI managed platform offers a free tier; Pro and Enterprise plans are available with custom pricing based on evaluation volume.
tools.best_for: Teams for whom output quality and safety evaluation are the primary concern, particularly those needing rigorous, research-backed metrics integrated into both development and production monitoring

cost_tips: Implement prompt caching and request deduplication: Tools like Helicone offer built-in caching so identical or near-identical requests return stored responses rather than hitting the API again, which can cut costs dramatically for applications with repetitive queries or shared user inputs.

Right-size your model selection per task: Use smaller, cheaper models (e.g., GPT-4o-mini, Claude Haiku) for straightforward classification or extraction tasks, and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning. Observability tools that log per-request model usage and cost make it easy to identify where expensive models are being used unnecessarily.

Set token budgets and monitor prompt bloat: Long system prompts, excessive few-shot examples, and verbose context windows are a leading cause of runaway token costs. Regularly audit average input and output token counts in your observability dashboard and trim prompts aggressively — even a 20% reduction in average prompt length compounds significantly at scale.

Use trace data to identify and eliminate low-value LLM calls: Production traces often reveal redundant agent steps, retry loops, or fallback chains that call the LLM multiple times for tasks that could be handled with a single optimized prompt or a non-LLM function. Reviewing traces in tools like Langfuse, LangSmith, or Arize regularly surfaces these inefficiencies before they become significant budget line items.
